text:
mike: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak i see p95 creep on the premium routes. baseline was 180ms, now we're seeing spikes ~260-320ms for short requests (<= 64 tokens). anyone else?
anya: saw it too, opened a perf trace. looks like batches are getting glued together past the target token budget. microbatch seam looks off.
lee: fwiw the selector change favours fused attention kernels for long sequences, but it seems to prefer them even when sequence is short and batch size winds up larger. could be cost estimate bug.
perf-bot: upload: /perf/traces/2364509123/trace.json.gz (10MB)
mike: attaching the quick diff: we changed kernel_costs['fused_attn'] from 0.9 -> 0.7 in selector, and lowered per-route token-budget margin for tier=gold from 0.15 -> 0.05.
anya: that combo explains it — lower margin + cheaper fused kernel -> batcher pulls more tokens into a slot, pushing microbatches over the p95 envelope.
lee: also noticed more KV cache evictions on those routes. prefix reuse rate dropped ~8% in the window. evictions lead to more compute per token, hurting short-tail latencies.
natalie: can we roll back the kernel cost change only to confirm? rolling back margin is riskier for throughput.
sam: quick repro: run 1k small chat reqs against gold route with kernel override:
```
REQS=1000
./loadtest --route gold --seq 32 --kernel fused_attn
```
I see median ok but p95 jumps to 300ms.
mike: @lee can you add logging for the selector decision (reason code) + chosen kernel and predicted cost per-token? want to see why fused gets chosen for seq=32.
lee: will add a cheap tag in selector: reason=(cost_est<alt_cost*0.95) and emit kernel_hint. deploying a canary now to canary-hosts.
perf-bot: canary deploy queued -> infra-bot: canary started on hosts r-12,r-13.
anya: observed an interesting side-effect: queue-policy "elastic-slice" is allocating token budgets by route TTL instead of current queue depth. that made it slow to retract budgets once load dips. contributes to prolonged p95.
mike: ok plan: 1) revert fused_attn cost tweak on canary, 2) instrument selector reason code + kernel_hint, 3) patch elastic-slice to consider short-term qps derivative (dQ/dt) so budgets scale down faster, 4) run A/B for 1 hour and collect traces.
natalie: agree. also add a kv-cache stat: prefix_hit_ratio per-route in perf dashboard so we can correlate evictions -> latency.
lee: pushed selector logging to canary (r-12). logs look like: `selector: seq=32 route=gold alt_cost=0.82 fused_cost=0.68 reason=estimated_end2end` — will try forcing fused_cost back to 0.9.
sam: running loadtest against canary now. initial 5m window: p95 dropped back from 310ms -> 195ms after forcing fused_cost=0.9. median unchanged.
mike: great. after the rollback let's also add a safeguard in the batcher: when route.p95_slo_ms < 250, enforce token_budget_margin >= 0.12. makes the governor SLO-aware.
anya: +1. we should add unit tests for budget shrink behavior: simulate sudden drop in qps and ensure budgets shrink within 2 collection intervals.
infra-bot: rollout: canary -> 50% traffic if metrics stable for 10m. monitoring alerts: p95, kv_eviction_rate, prefix_hit_ratio, selector_reason_counts.
perf-bot: saved trace: /perf/traces/2364509423/post-revert.json.gz (8.2MB)
mike: thanks all — i'll open an RFC for "elastic-slice SLO-aware derivative" and attach these traces. we'll follow up tomorrow with quantified numbers and a slow rollout plan. :thumbsup:
